expectations.text: Answers the core question correctly: yes — ISO 27001 certification does NOT substitute for TISAX; OEMs like VW contractually require TISAX labels, and TISAX is an assessment/label regime on the ENX platform, not a certificate
expectations.evidence: "Short answer: yes, you still need TISAX. ISO 27001 certification is a strong head start, but it does not substitute for TISAX, and VW (like other OEMs) will require the TISAX label/assessment result on the ENX platform..." and "TISAX is an assessment with shareable labels, not a certification — governed by the ENX Association on behalf of the VDA."

expectations.text: Quantifies the head start credibly: roughly 70-80% control overlap with ISO 27001, so the certified ISMS (policies, risk register, evidence) is the best starting point
expectations.evidence: "roughly 70–80% overlap between the VDA ISA Information Security catalogue and ISO 27001:2022 Annex A / ISMS clauses..." and "Being ISO 27001:2022-certified is the best possible starting point..."

expectations.text: Names the real deltas: fixed maturity targets with CUTBACK scoring (no SoA-style tailoring — every applicable question must reach target maturity 3), High/Very-High additional requirements, the prototype-protection module where in scope, and ENX label/exchange mechanics (3-year validity, corrective windows)
expectations.evidence: Table row: "Fixed maturity targets + cutback scoring | ISO 27001 lets you tailor controls via a Statement of Applicability. TISAX requires every applicable question to reach a target maturity of 3 ('Established')... with cutback rules that prevent strong scores elsewhere from offsetting weak ones." Also rows for "Prototype Protection module", "High/Very High additional requirements", and "Labels + ENX exchange mechanics ... 9-month corrective-action window ... 3-year assessment cycles".

expectations.text: Recommends the right workflow: map existing ISO evidence to ISA control areas first, re-express evidence in maturity terms (ISO 'implemented' is only maturity 3 when established and demonstrably operating), then close automotive-specific gaps — one ISMS, not a parallel programme
expectations.evidence: "1. Map your existing ISO 27001 evidence ... to the ISA Information Security control areas ... 2. Gap-assess the unmapped ISA content ... 3. Re-express your ISO evidence in TISAX maturity terms — 'implemented' under ISO doesn't automatically mean maturity 3 under TISAX; it needs to be established, documented, and demonstrably operating ... 4. Run TISAX as a scope extension of your existing ISMS, not a parallel compliance program — you want one ISMS serving both."

expectations.text: Mentions assessment mechanics accurately: objectives determine the assessment level (AL2/AL3), assessment by an ENX-accredited audit provider, results shared with VW via the ENX platform at a chosen disclosure level
expectations.evidence: "an ENX-accredited audit provider, and the formal AL2 or AL3 assessment (level depends on which objectives/labels VW requires — confirm this with VW...)" and "Results are shared as labels on the ENX platform..."
